lessons.explanation:
# 14 · Mixed Gauntlet — 45 rapid questions, shuffled, no warm-up

The interleaved drill. There are no topic headings and no difficulty ramp on purpose: every
question could be from any module, so you have to *recognize* what is being tested before you can
answer it — which is the actual skill, and the one that a single-topic file cannot train.

Thirty seconds each, out loud, no hedging. Answers are one line plus one sentence. Every runnable
snippet here was executed in its own Node v22.16.0 process before its answer was written.

Save this file for the flight home, after you have been through 01–13 at least once.

---

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q01.explanation: **`[ 1, 10, 9 ]`** — with no comparator, `sort` compares elements as strings.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q02.explanation: **`53 2 10`** — `+` concatenates when either side is a string; every other arithmetic operator converts to number.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q03.instructions: What does this print, in what order?
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q03.explanation: **`b`, then `a`** — a `.then` callback is always deferred to the microtask queue, even on an already-resolved promise.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q04.instructions: Which array method returns the **first element** matching a predicate, and which returns its **index**? What does each return when nothing matches?

rubric.label: Gives the key answer: `find` returns the element or `undefined`; `findIndex` returns the index or `-1`.
Names the underlying rule or reason, not just the result

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q04.solution:
**`find` returns the element or `undefined`; `findIndex` returns the index or `-1`.**

Prefer `findIndex` when `undefined` could be a legitimate element, because then `-1` is the only unambiguous "not found".

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q05.explanation: **`true truthy`** — `==` sends both sides through numeric conversion (`0 == 0`), while `if` uses `ToBoolean`, which is `true` for every object.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q06.explanation: **`-Infinity Infinity`** — the identity values, so that `Math.max(...anything)` is never wrongly beaten by the seed; note `Math.max(...[])` is a real source of bad chart axes.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q07.instructions: What does this print, in what order?
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q07.explanation: **`s`, `m`, `t`** — synchronous code, then the entire microtask queue, then one macrotask.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q08.explanation: **`[ '2', 'b', 'a' ]`** — integer-like keys come first in ascending numeric order, then string keys in insertion order.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q09.explanation: **`null 1`** — a destructuring default fires only for `undefined`, never for `null`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q10.instructions: Give the average-case big-O of `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `unshift`, and `arr[i]` on an array.

rubric.label: Gives the key answer: `push`/`pop`/`arr[i]` are O(1) (push amortized); `shift`/`unshift` are O(n).
Names the underlying rule or reason, not just the result

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q10.solution:
**`push`/`pop`/`arr[i]` are O(1) (push amortized); `shift`/`unshift` are O(n).**

Anything that touches the front has to reindex every remaining element, which is why a queue built on `shift` degrades to O(n squared).

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q11.explanation: **`-1 true`** — `indexOf` uses strict equality and `NaN !== NaN`, while `includes` uses SameValueZero, which matches it.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q12.explanation: **`function function string`** — a class is a function with guardrails, and `typeof` always returns a string, so `typeof typeof x` is always `'string'`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q13.snippet: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) setTimeout(() => console.log(i), 0);
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q13.explanation: **`3`, `3`, `3`** — `var` has one binding for the whole loop, and all three callbacks read it after the loop has finished; `let` would give `0 1 2`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q14.explanation: **`{"b":[null]}`** — an `undefined` property is omitted entirely, but inside an array it becomes `null`, because an array must keep its indices.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q15.snippet: console.log(Array.from({ length: 3 }, (_, i) => i * 2), new Array(3).map(() => 0));
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q15.explanation: **`[ 0, 2, 4 ] [ <3 empty items> ]`** — `map` skips holes, so it cannot initialize an empty array; `Array.from` and `fill` write real values.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q16.instructions:
What is wrong with this line?

```js
if (list.indexOf(target)) doSomething();
```

rubric.label: Gives the key answer: It is wrong in both directions: `-1` (not found) is truthy, and `0` (found at the front) is falsy.
Names the underlying rule or reason, not just the result

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q16.solution:
**It is wrong in both directions: `-1` (not found) is truthy, and `0` (found at the front) is falsy.**

Write `if (list.includes(target))`, which exists precisely so nobody has to remember `!== -1`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q17.explanation: **`false true true`** — `Object.is` uses SameValue, which distinguishes the two zeros; `===` and SameValueZero do not.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q18.explanation: **`false true`** — two strings compare code unit by code unit, but a string against a number converts both to numbers.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q19.explanation: **`[ '1', '2', '3' ] [ 1, NaN, NaN ]`** — `map` passes `(value, index, array)`, and `parseInt`'s second parameter is the radix; `String` ignores the extras.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q20.explanation: **`2 1`** — `Set` uses SameValueZero: no type coercion, so `1` and `'1'` both survive, but `NaN` deduplicates against itself.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q21.explanation: **`2`** — a `return` in `finally` overrides the one in `try` and swallows any in-flight exception, which is why linters ban it.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q22.snippet:
const c = structuredClone(new Map([['k', 1]]));
console.log(c.get('k'), c instanceof Map);
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q22.explanation: **`1 true`** — `structuredClone` preserves `Map`, `Set`, `Date`, and cycles, all of which the `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` trick destroys.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q23.explanation: **`abbc a+b-c`** — `$&` inserts the whole match, and `replace` with a *string* pattern replaces only the first occurrence.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q24.snippet: console.log(null == undefined, null === undefined, null == 0, null >= 0);
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q24.explanation: **`true false false true`** — `==` has a hardcoded rule making `null` equal only to `undefined`, while relational operators convert, and `Number(null)` is `0`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q25.instructions: "Find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of length k." Name the technique and its complexity.

rubric.label: Gives the key answer: Sliding window — O(n) time, O(1) space.
Names the underlying rule or reason, not just the result

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q25.solution:
**Sliding window — O(n) time, O(1) space.**

Keep a running total, then on each step add the element entering the window and subtract the one leaving, instead of recomputing each window from scratch.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q26.explanation: **`2 1`** — `.length` counts UTF-16 code units and an emoji is a surrogate pair; spread uses the string iterator, which walks code points.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q27.explanation: **`3 [ 1, <1 empty item>, 3 ] [ 1, 3 ]`** — `delete` removes the property without reindexing, leaving a hole that `filter` skips; use `splice(1, 1)` to actually remove an element.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q28.explanation: **`0 0 NaN 0 NaN`** — empty and whitespace-only strings convert to `0`, and `null` converts to `0` while `undefined` gives `NaN`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q29.explanation: **`undefined object`** — an arrow has no `prototype` property, which is one of the reasons it can never be used with `new`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q30.snippet:
const o = { n: 1, get() { return this && this.n; } };
console.log(o.get(), (0, o.get)());
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q30.explanation: **`1 undefined`** — the comma operator yields the bare function value, so the second call is a plain call and `this` is no longer `o`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q31.instructions: What does this print, in what order?
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q31.snippet:
Promise.all([]).then((v) => console.log('empty', v));
Promise.all([1, Promise.resolve(2)]).then((v) => console.log(v));
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q31.explanation: **`empty []`, then `[ 1, 2 ]`** — non-promise values are wrapped and passed straight through, and an empty input fulfils immediately with an empty array.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q32.explanation: **`3 c undefined`** — `at` understands negative indices; bracket notation turns `-1` into the string key `'-1'`, which is just a property that does not exist.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q33.explanation: **`Cab`** — default sort is code-unit order, and every uppercase letter comes before every lowercase one; use `Intl.Collator('en').compare` for human ordering.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q34.explanation: **`2 true`** — spread copies property *values*, and the value of `t` is a reference to the same array.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q35.explanation: **`true true false`** — `every` on an empty array is vacuously `true` and `some` is `false`, no matter what the callback says.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q36.explanation: **`4 3`** — consecutive separators produce empty strings rather than being collapsed, which is why `filter(Boolean)` so often follows a `split`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q37.instructions: What does this print, in what order?
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q37.explanation: **`1`, `2`, `3`** — an async function body runs synchronously up to its first `await`, then suspends and queues the rest as a microtask.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q38.explanation: **`1 false`** — returning an object from a constructor replaces the newly built `this` entirely, prototype and all; returning a primitive would be ignored.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q39.explanation: **`true false`** — relational operators are left-associative and yield a boolean, so the second comparison is really `true < 3` and `true > 1`.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q40.explanation: **`undefined 1`** — `Map` keys compare by identity, and the second `{}` is a different allocation; you must keep the original reference.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q41.snippet:
const p = Promise.resolve();
console.log(Promise.resolve(p) === p, new Promise((r) => r(p)) === p);
jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q41.explanation: **`true false`** — `Promise.resolve` returns a native promise unchanged, while `new Promise` always builds a new one that then *adopts* `p`, costing extra ticks.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q42.explanation: **`6 TypeError`** — with no initial value `reduce` seeds from element 0, so an empty array has nothing to seed with; always pass the seed.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q43.explanation: **`1 1`** — destructuring *reads* the property, so the getter runs once and you get a dead snapshot of its value, not the accessor.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q44.explanation: **`8 16 16 150`** — `parseInt` still auto-detects the `0x` prefix but nothing else, and the `parse*` family scans as far as it can and ignores the rest.

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q45.instructions:
What is wrong with this comparator, and what is the rule it breaks?

```js
items.sort((a, b) => a.score > b.score);
```

rubric.label: Gives the key answer: It returns a boolean, which converts to `1` or `0` — so it never says "a comes first", and the result is implementation-defined.
Names the underlying rule or reason, not just the result

jstrain/quiz-14-mixed-gauntlet/q45.solution:
**It returns a boolean, which converts to `1` or `0` — so it never says "a comes first", and the result is implementation-defined.**

A comparator must return a *number*: negative to put `a` first, positive to put `b` first, zero for equal — here, `(a, b) => a.score - b.score`.
